Latent Variable Model

We can use a dimension reduction technique to create correlation between stocks by building a covariance matrix with latent factor loading. That sounds complicated but is relatively straightforward to code. See gllvm for an R package that does that.

If we want the error for some stocks to be correlated, then for year \(t\), across all stocks,

\[ \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \Sigma), \] where \(\Sigma\) is a covariance matrix. We can induce a flexible low dimension covariance matrix by adding some unique random effects such that for some unobserved variables per year \(z_t\), and factor loading \(\lambda_s\) per stock, then

\[ \mathbf{z}_i \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \text{I}). \] We will start with two latent variables, and write

\[ \log(R_i/S_i) = \alpha_{s_i} + \beta_{s_i} S_i + \mathbf{z}_{t}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{s_i} + \epsilon_i \]

library(RTMB)

sox$stock <- as.numeric(factor(sox$PopName))
nstocks <- max(sox$stock)
sox <- sox %>% mutate(time = yr - min(yr) + 1)
nyears <- max(sox$time)
minyear <- min(sox$yr)
sox$logRS <- log(sox$recruits/sox$spawners)
nobs <- nrow(sox)

parameters <- list(
  alpha0 = runif(1, 2, 5),
  re = rnorm(nstocks),
  logbeta = runif(nstocks, 0, 1),
  logsigma = runif(nstocks, 3, 5),
  logsigma_re = runif(1, 0.5, 2),
  re_time = rnorm(nyears),
  logitphi = 0,
  logsigma_time = 0,
  z = matrix(0, nrow = nyears, ncol = 2),
  logsigma_z = c(0,0),
  lambda1 = c(1, rnorm(nstocks-1)),
  lambda2 = c(0,1, rnorm(nstocks-2))
)

negll <- function(pars){
  
  getAll(pars, sox, warn = FALSE)
  beta <- exp(logbeta)
  
  logRS <- OBS(logRS)

  sigma <- exp(logsigma)
  sigma_re <- exp(logsigma_re)
  sigma_time <- exp(logsigma_time)
  sigma_obs <- sigma[stock]
  sigma_z <- exp(logsigma_z)
  phi <- 2*plogis(logitphi)-1
  
  alpha_stock <- re + alpha0
  ADREPORT(alpha_stock)
  
  mu <- AD(numeric(nobs))
  for( i in 1:nobs ){
    mu[i] <- alpha_stock[stock[i]] + re_time[time[i]] - beta[stock[i]]*spawners_scaled[i] + 
      z[time[i],1]*lambda1[stock[i]]*sigma_z[1] + z[time[i],2]*lambda2[stock[i]]*sigma_z[2]
  }
  
  ## Use this for built in residuals
  ll <- dautoreg(re_time,phi=phi,scale=sqrt(sigma_time^2/(1-phi^2)), log=TRUE)
  ## Add in latent variables
  for( i in 1:2 ) ll <- ll + sum(dnorm(z[,i], 0, 1, log = TRUE))
    
  
  ll <- ll + sum(dnorm(re, 0, sigma_re, log = TRUE))
  ll <- ll + sum(dnorm(logRS, mu, sigma_obs, log = TRUE))
  
  REPORT(mu)
  REPORT(re_time)
  REPORT(sigma_obs)
  
  return(-ll)
}

obj <- MakeADFun(func = negll, parameters = parameters, random = c("re", "re_time", "z"), 
  map = list(lambda1 = factor(c(NA, 2:nstocks)), lambda2 = factor(c(NA, NA, 3:nstocks))), 
  silent = TRUE)
fit <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
sox$expected <- obj$report()$mu
sox$sigma <- obj$report()$sigma_obs
sox <- sox %>% 
  mutate(resid = logRS - expected) %>%
  mutate(resid_std = resid/sigma)

ggplot(data = sox, aes(x = expected, y = resid)) + 
  geom_point() + theme_minimal() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, col = 'red', linetype = 2) +
  ylab("Observed - Expected")

## Stock Covariance
## Extract fitted parameters
p <- obj$env$parList(fit$par)

## Factor loading matrix
Lambda <- cbind(p$lambda1, p$lambda2)

## Covariance between stocks
Sigma_latent <- Lambda %*% t(Lambda)

library(corrplot)
Warning: package 'corrplot' was built under R version 4.4.3
corrplot 0.95 loaded
corrplot(
  cov2cor(Sigma_latent),
  method = "color",
  type = "lower",
  addCoef.col = "black",
  tl.col = "black",
  title = "Latent correlation between stocks",
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0)
)

## Convert to correlation
Cor_latent <- cov2cor(Sigma_latent)

## Convert correlation to Euclidean distance
D <- as.dist(sqrt(2 * (1 - Cor_latent)))

## Fit PAM for different numbers of clusters
k_range <- 2:min(10, nstocks - 1)

library(cluster)

pam_fits <- lapply(k_range, function(k) {
  pam(D, k = k, diss = TRUE)
})

## Average silhouette widths
sil_width <- sapply(pam_fits, function(x) {
  x$silinfo$avg.width
})

## Optimal number of clusters
best_k <- k_range[which.max(sil_width)]

best_k
[1] 8
plot(
  k_range,
  sil_width,
  type = "b",
  pch = 19,
  xlab = "Number of clusters",
  ylab = "Average silhouette width",
  main = "Choosing number of clusters"
)

abline(v = best_k, col = "red", lty = 2)

pam_best <- pam_fits[[which(k_range == best_k)]]

stock_clusters <- pam_best$clustering

output <- data.frame(stock = 1:nstocks, stock_cluster = stock_clusters)
sox <- sox %>% left_join(output)
